newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Life to convert to public company.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Life to convert to public company.

text.p: Swiss Life/Rentenanstalt said its supervisory board reached a definitive decision to convert into a public limited company from its present form of cooperative.

As soon as the transformation is completed the cooperative members, some 600,000 insurance clients, will become shareholders and be allocated 6.18 million shares free of charge, the company said in a statement.

As part of the arrangement, Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) will acquire a 25 percent stake in Swiss Life/Rentenanstalt. To this end granted UBS has granted Swiss Life a convertible bond issue which will be converted into a shareholding following the legal form modification.
Swiss Life and UBS have worked together since January 1, 1996 through a joint subsidiary called UBS Swiss Life.
Swiss Life also said holders of participation certificates will vote on February 20 on the resolution to convert participation capital into share capital.
Cooperative members will vote on the plan to convert to a public limited company between May 26 and June 20.
If the plan wins approval by a two-thirds margin then the company will be registered on June 30, 1997, Swiss Life said.
Following the conversion to a public company Swiss Life said it would have share capital of 391.57 million francs and conditional capital through the convertible bond of another 195.78 million.
The total capital of 587.35 billion will comprise 11,747,000 bearer shares with a nominal value of 50 francs each. -- Zurich Editorial +41 631 7340
